newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-PACK WAS TOO TENTATIVE, ADMITS LIONS COACH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-PACK WAS TOO TENTATIVE, ADMITS LIONS COACH.

text.p: Assistant coach Jim Telfer admitted on Sunday the British Lions' pack was too tentative in their opening tour match against an Eastern Province Invitation XV.
The Lions won the match 39-11 on Saturday but were criticised by the home side as being vulnerable in the forwards.
"I thought we were quite tentative in our set piece play but we haven't practised that much or played together before," admitted Telfer.

"The lineout wasn't as good as we hoped it would be, although I thought we competed quite well on their ball. The scrums were a bit tentative as well and we tended to get wheeled but I thought we held their scrum quite well."
Jaco Kirsten, captain of the Eastern Province side, said he believed the Lions' front five lacked physical strength and that the South Africans should attack them through the pack.

Lions lock and skipper Martin Johnson, who did not play in Saturday's match, responded: "The South African coaches, players and their press are going to say things like that but we are just going to have get on with our own game."
Telfer added: "They can say what they like. It's the same when you play in New Zealand -- you will get comments like that -- but we will certainly be looking to improve.

"Our body positions were good but there's quite a lot of work to be done in the set pieces and the aggressive dynamism in the loose. We are not satisfied but then we will never be completely satisfied."
Centre Scott Gibbs and loose forward Tim Rodber (illness) and wing John Bentley (toe injury) trained on Sunday morning and will be fit to play against Border in the Lions' second match on Wednesday.
Prop Tom Smith reported a neck spasm after Saturday's game but it is expected to clear in a couple of days.
